title: Transformers & LLM Training Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on the transformer architecture, tokenization, next-token prediction, attention, context windows, and the pretraining, instruction tuning and RLHF pipeline.

chapters.title: Transformer Mental Model
points: A transformer is a stack of identical blocks, each with self-attention then a feed-forward network, wrapped in residual connections and layer norm
Decoder-only models (GPT, Claude, Llama) generate text left to right; encoder-only (BERT) reads both directions for understanding tasks
Embeddings turn token IDs into vectors; positional information is added so word order is not lost
Each block refines the vector for every token; the final layer's vector is projected to scores (logits) over the vocabulary
Parallel processing of all tokens during training is why transformers beat RNNs, which process sequentially

chapters.title: Tokens and Next-Token Prediction
points: A token is a sub-word chunk (BPE merges frequent byte pairs); roughly 4 characters or 0.75 English words per token
Tokenization is deterministic text-to-ID mapping done before the model; the model never sees raw characters
Letter counting, arithmetic and non-English text suffer because words split into odd or many tokens
The model outputs logits, softmax turns them into a probability distribution over the vocabulary, and one token is sampled
Temperature rescales logits (low = near-greedy, high = diverse); top-k and top-p cut the candidate set before sampling
Generation is autoregressive: each sampled token is appended to the input and the loop repeats until a stop token

chapters.title: Attention Mechanism
points: Each token produces a Query, Key and Value vector; attention scores are softmax(QKᵀ/√d) and the output is the weighted sum of Values
Dividing by √d keeps dot products small so softmax does not saturate and kill gradients
Causal masking blocks each token from attending to later tokens, which makes next-token training valid
Multi-head attention runs several attention operations in parallel so heads can learn different relations, then concatenates them
Self-attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length (n²), the root of long-context expense
KV cache stores past Keys and Values during generation so each new token costs one step instead of recomputing everything

chapters.title: Context Windows in Practice
points: The context window is the maximum tokens of input plus output the model can attend to at once; exceeding it truncates or errors
Input and output share the window, so a long prompt shrinks the room left for the answer
The model has no memory between calls; the whole conversation is resent each turn and you pay for it every time
Information in the middle of a very long prompt is recalled worse than at the start or end (lost in the middle)
A bigger window is not a substitute for retrieval; long inputs cost more, run slower and dilute attention
Prompt caching reuses a repeated prefix to cut latency and cost, so put stable content first

chapters.title: Pretraining, Instruction Tuning and RLHF
points: Pretraining: next-token prediction on huge raw text yields a base model that completes text but does not follow instructions
Instruction tuning (SFT): fine-tune on prompt-response pairs so the model follows instructions and answers in the desired format
RLHF: humans rank outputs, a reward model learns those preferences, then PPO-style reinforcement learning optimizes the model against it
DPO skips the separate reward model and trains directly on preference pairs, which is simpler and more stable
Pretraining gives knowledge, SFT gives format and behavior, RLHF aligns with helpfulness and safety; RLHF does not add new facts
Common mistakes: expecting a base model to chat, assuming fine-tuning reliably teaches new knowledge, and reward hacking (the model games the reward model)

chapters.title: Transformers Cheat Sheet
points: Pipeline: text → tokens → embeddings → N × (attention + FFN) → logits → softmax → sample → append → repeat
Attention = softmax(QKᵀ/√d)·V, causal mask for generation, cost O(n²) in sequence length
Sampling knobs: temperature (sharpness), top-k (fixed count), top-p (probability mass)
Context window = input + output tokens; resent every turn; keep stable prefix first for caching
Training stages: pretrain (knowledge) → SFT (instruction following) → RLHF/DPO (preference alignment)
